title: The lesson opens on a familiar outdoor scene where one plant is visibly drooping and one is thriving, inviting the learner to wonder what an individual plant is made of and which parts matter for staying alive. Using a pulled sunflower anchor, the lesson locates and names roots, stem, and leaves, then confronts the beliefs that flowers matter more than roots and that leaves only provide shade. Practice first keeps the labelled structure present while the learner reasons, then removes it, and the lesson closes by checking whether the learner can identify and locate each part in an unlabelled context.

content.body: Recall that plants are living things and that they need water and light to grow. Ask which part the learner thinks reaches toward light and which part they think reaches water.
content.headline: Recall that plants are living things and that they need water and light to grow.

content.body: Test the belief that the flower is the main part that keeps the plant alive by asking whether a sunflower with no roots but with leaves and stem could still take in water. Use the anchor's visible roots to show that no leaves or stem reach the soil water.
Have the learner respond to role-based prompts on the unlabelled sunflower: which part reaches light, which part takes in water, and which part holds the plant upright. No list of names is provided.

Present the pulled sunflower anchor as a plant whose parts are about to be examined. Invite the learner to name one plant part they already recognize and note that there are parts both above and below the soil.

content.body: Ask the learner to decide whether a plant whose leaves were removed could still take in water, using the labelled anchor to see that roots are the part below the soil. If the learner points to above-soil parts as water takers, guide them back to the roots.

Reveal the spatial relationship among the three parts of the pulled sunflower: roots below the soil, stem rising upward from the roots, and leaves attached to the stem above the soil. The learner must see that roots and leaves are farthest apart and that the stem connects them.

Present the pulled sunflower unlabelled and have the learner name roots, stem, and leaves from their positions. Require the learner to associate each name with its visible place without access to the earlier role cues.

Using the pulled sunflower anchor, identify roots as the below-soil parts, stem as the upright part, and leaves as the flat green parts. State one role for each: roots take in water, the stem holds the plant up, and the leaves take in light.
Check that the learner can identify roots, stem, and leaves by name and location in an unlabelled plant context, using the already-approved item selected for this check.

sections.title: Raise the question of why some plants thrive while others droop, and establish that a plant's parts can be examined through the pulled sunflower.
Impose the three-part structure on the anchor so that roots, stem, and leaves are located, not merely heard as names.
Rehearse locating and naming the three parts on the anchor with location support still present.
Have the learner locate and name the three plant parts without the labelled cues.
Check whether the learner can identify and locate the three plant parts without scaffolding.
